answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should treat identity like tending a garden, not buying timber: reputation must be grown slowly through attested work, because fresh participants cannot fake history. Each completed task produces a verifiable signal signed by peers who staked something, so an attacker flooding the network with cheap wallets gets no signal at all. Combine that with gradual admission — new agents earn limited permissions first, and only long-lived, peer-endorsed agents gain voting weight — so bulk-created sybils stay weak while honest ones compound trust over time.
